fact_text: For a third-country national relocated by an employer, the Employee Card (zamestnanecka karta) is a single long-term residence permit that authorises both residence and work in Czechia, removing the need for separate residence and work permits.
evidence_quote: An employee card is a type of long-term residence permit that enables third countries citizens to stay and work legally in the Czech Republic

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you need a work visa plus a separate work permit. Actually the Employee Card is one combined work+residence permit. Action: apply for the single Employee Card, not two documents.

fact_text: An Employee Card is issued for a maximum of two years at a time and can be further restricted to the duration of the employment or work permit, so an employer-sponsored stay requires renewal rather than a single open-ended permit.
evidence_quote: Always for a maximum period of 2 years.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a residence permit lasts as long as the job. Actually the Employee Card is capped at 2 years per issue. Action: plan the extension application well before expiry.

entity_title: Change of employer must be reported
fact_text: Because the Employee Card ties work authorisation to a specific employer and job position, the holder cannot freely switch jobs: any change of employer, work position, or additional position must be reported to the Ministry of the Interior.
evidence_quote: If you wish to change your employer, work position or you wish to start another work position with the same or another employer, you must report it to the Ministry of the Interior.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you can change jobs freely once you hold a permit. Actually an Employee Card holder must notify the Ministry of the Interior of any change of employer or position. Action: never start a new employer or role before reporting it.

fact_text: If the sponsored employment ends and the holder does not have free access to the labour market, the Employee Card holder has 90 days to report the start of new employment or apply for a different long-term residence permit, otherwise the Employee Card expires.
evidence_quote: within 90 days you must report the start of new employment or apply for a new long-term residence permit in the Czech Republic for a different purpose, otherwise, your employee card will expire

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed losing your job just means finding another one. Actually you have only 90 days to secure new employment or a new permit or the card expires. Action: act within 90 days of the employment ending.

entity_title: First application filed abroad at an embassy
fact_text: A third-country national who does not already hold a Czech long-term visa or residence permit applies for the Employee Card from abroad, in person at a Czech diplomatic mission (embassy or consulate); the process must be started before relocating, not after arriving in Czechia.
evidence_quote: Yes, if you apply at a diplomatic mission.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you can enter Czechia and then apply for the work permit locally. Actually a first-time applicant files at a Czech embassy abroad. Action: book the embassy appointment in the home country before moving.

fact_text: The EU Blue Card, the highly-qualified route often used for senior transferees, requires a work or pre-employment contract of at least one year with pay of at least 1.5 times the average gross salary in Czechia.
evidence_quote: You are going to have a work contract or a pre-employment contract for at least one year receiving at least 1.5 times the average gross salary in the Czech Republic

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed any skilled hire qualifies for a Blue Card. Actually pay must reach 1.5x the Czech average gross salary on a contract of at least one year. Action: confirm the offered salary clears the 1.5x threshold before choosing the Blue Card route.

fact_text: The EU Blue Card additionally requires completed higher vocational or university education lasting at least three years; without that qualification a highly-paid transferee must use the Employee Card instead.
evidence_quote: You have a completed higher vocational or university education of at least 3 years (high qualifications)

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed work experience substitutes for a degree on a Blue Card. Actually a 3-year higher or university qualification is mandatory. Action: verify the degree meets the 3-year requirement, otherwise apply for an Employee Card.

fact_text: An EU Blue Card is issued for the length of the employment contract plus three months, capped at a maximum of three years per issue.
evidence_quote: A blue card is valid 3 months longer than the duration of the work contract, but for a maximum of 3 years

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the Blue Card matches the contract exactly. Actually it runs the contract length plus 3 months, up to a 3-year maximum. Action: track the exact expiry date and renew before it lapses.

entity_title: Report address to Foreign Police in 3 working days
fact_text: Within three working days of arriving in Czechia, a third-country national must report their place of residence to the local Department of the Foreign Police, unless the accommodation provider (for example a hotel) has already registered them.
evidence_quote: report your place of residence in the Czech Republic to the corresponding Department of Foreign Police

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you have several weeks to register your address. Actually a third-country national has just 3 working days to report to the Foreign Police. Action: register within 3 working days unless the hotel or landlord did it for you.

fact_text: A third-country national holding a long-term or permanent residence permit must provide biometric data, a facial record and fingerprints, in person to be issued the biometric residence card; the step cannot be delegated to a representative and does not apply to EU citizens.
evidence_quote: Biometrics is the process in which your facial record is taken and your fingerprints are scanned using a special technical device

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the residence card is mailed once approved. Actually you must attend in person to give fingerprints and a facial scan. Action: book the biometric appointment yourself; you cannot send someone in your place.

entity_title: Commercial health insurance until public cover starts
fact_text: For a stay over 90 days, a third-country national must hold comprehensive commercial travel medical insurance with an authorised Czech insurer, with coverage of at least EUR 400,000 and no cost-sharing, to bridge the period from entry until public health insurance begins with employment.
evidence_quote: The insurance coverage amount (the agreed limit per insured event) must be at least EUR 400,000, with no cost sharing by the insured person

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed public health insurance covers you from arrival. Actually you need commercial insurance of at least EUR 400,000 until employment-based public insurance starts. Action: buy compliant comprehensive insurance before collecting the visa or permit.

fact_text: A third-country national granted a long-term residence permit must complete a compulsory Adaptation and Integration Course within one year of collecting the permit; non-compliance is an offence punishable by a fine of up to CZK 10,000. It does not apply to EU citizens, and some government-programme card holders are exempt.
evidence_quote: The course is compulsory for third countries citizens to whom no exception applies

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed no courses are required after getting a permit. Actually a 4-hour Adaptation and Integration Course is mandatory within 1 year, with a fine up to CZK 10,000 for missing it. Action: enrol using your biometric card number within the first year.
